observations.evidence: Phase 2 step 2 ran `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/dev feat/gap_bugs_fixer` and got exit code 129 with stderr `usage: git merge-tree <base-tree> <branch1> <branch2>`. `git --version` returned `git version 2.37.0.windows.1`; the `--write-tree` form requires git 2.38+. Skill fell back to a worktree probe (`git worktree add --detach $TMPDIR origin/dev` + `git merge --no-commit --no-ff <head>`), which produced the equivalent verdict (`Automatic merge went well; stopped before committing as requested`, exit=0, no unmerged paths). Run 2 (2026-05-08) also hit this — its run-history notes record `legacy 3-arg git merge-tree because git 2.37 lacks --write-tree; exit=0, empty stdout` — but no matching observation was filed.
observations.interpretation: The SKILL.md prescribes a command (`git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only ...`) that fails on git versions the operator actually runs. Each run requires ad-hoc fallback. Proper remediation is a Phase 2 sub-step: `git --version | parse → if >=2.38 use --write-tree; else use worktree probe (git worktree add --detach + git merge --no-commit --no-ff + read git diff --diff-filter=U; cleanup with git worktree remove --force)`. Observer count: 1 in observations.json. Real-world count: 2 (this run + 2026-05-08 noted in run_history but not seeded). No proposal at threshold yet, but a third recurrence should trip the convergence rule once another improvement_suggestions[] entry with a matching tag lands.

observations.evidence: Phase 7 item #3 was resolved as `Auto-fix now`. Ran `docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml run --rm --entrypoint=ruff backend check --fix <files>` and got `E902 Read-only file system (os error 30)` for every changed file — `docker-compose.test.yml` mounts source as `./backend/intelligence_platform:/app/intelligence_platform:ro` and `./backend/tests:/app/tests:ro`. Skill fell back to a manual `docker run` with rw mount overrides and `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` for git-bash on Windows: `docker run --rm -v /c/.../backend/intelligence_platform:/app/intelligence_platform:rw -v .../backend/tests:/app/tests:rw -v .../backend/pyproject.toml:/app/pyproject.toml:ro -w //app intelligence-platform-test-backend ruff check --fix <files>` → `Found 86 errors (59 fixed, 27 remaining)`.
observations.interpretation: Test-stack compose deliberately mounts source read-only (so tests cannot mutate working tree), which conflicts with any Phase 7 'auto-fix now' resolution that wants to modify the source. Per the observer's narrow exception, this is environmental friction with no clean SKILL.md fix — the test container is correctly read-only by design. The right remediation is operator-side: either run ruff against a local virtualenv (no ruff currently on host PATH per `which ruff` → exit 1), or document the rw-override docker invocation in the SKILL.md as the canonical Phase 7 auto-fix command. Recording in observations.json, not friction_log[], because a SKILL.md doc-edit is plausible (not strictly an environment-only issue).

The user then re-asked twice (`should we register this a gap or not , it is unclear what you recommend here and why`; `I need to undertand if we can fix this quilcy before proceeding`) before I explicitly recommended `#1 + #2 + #3(a)`.
observations.interpretation: Phase 7's resolution-options menu currently lists block / fix-now / skip / abort without any default-recommendation logic. For trivial in-session safe fixes (one-line additions, smoke-passing, no behavior change), the skill should default-recommend `fix-now` and order it visually first, instead of treating all four options symmetrically. The user's typed suggestion attests to this in the convergence-rule sense: ≥1 unaddressed observer observation (this one) + matching improvement_suggestions[] entry verbatim → cluster trips on first observer occurrence. Proposal will be written to suggestions.md.
